Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations on Wednesday, saying its financial situation was “critical” and it needed new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

In a press release on Thursday, PIA said: “Flight operations between Pakistan and the United Kingdom have been restored following yesterday’s cancellations by our wet-lease partner.”

The airline said its teams assisted all passengers in both London and Manchester and that passengers affected by the flight cancellations had been re-accommodated on subsequent flights “in accordance with their individual travel preferences”.

“Passengers who opted to alter or defer their travel plans due to the disruption have been facilitated with full, penalty-free refunds,” it added.

The statement said that in line with the contingency plan activated last night, the airline had “transitioned its UK operations directly onto its own widebody Boeing 777 fleet”.

“Today’s scheduled UK services and operations are running on schedule,” the airline added.

In yesterday’s statement, PIA said flights PK786 from London Heathrow to Islamabad, scheduled for 7:55pm GMT, and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore, scheduled for 7pm GMT, were cancelled.

“Notice of this operational suspension was communicated to PIA without any prior warning just as passengers were preparing to board their respective flights in London and Manchester,” the airline’s spokesperson said.

It termed the abrupt suspension of Norse Atlantic’s operations without notice “deeply regrettable” and said it was pursuing the matter with the carrier at the “highest contractual and executive levels”.

PIA was privatised in December last year through an auction. A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for a 75 per cent stake in the airline, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion. The Arif Habib-led consortium had vowed to transform the loss-making airline through operational restructuring, fleet expansion, and improved customer service.

In October, the airline signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the expansion of the airline’s fleet as it aims to meet rising demand.

Following Norse Atlantic’s announcement on Wednesday about its financial situation, its shares plummeted by 76 per cent at 1:03pm GMT. Most of the airline’s market value has already been wiped out this year.

The Norwegian company is now in talks to secure short-term financing, it said in a statement.

“However, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution,” Norse said. It did not say how long it could still operate without new financing.

The carrier, which does not hedge its jet fuel needs, cut capacity as costs skyrocketed following the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February. Many other airlines are faced with the same problem, filing for bankruptcy or initiating restructuring proceedings to survive.

articles.title: MNA among senior JUI-F leaders detained in Sargodha: police
articles.summary:
Several senior Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders were detained in Sargodha late on Wednesday, police said, prompting the party to demand their “immediate release”.

The developments come amid tensions between Fazl and the federal government, which have been ongoing since mid-October.

Sargodha Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Sukhera told Dawn that Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, a member of the National Assembly, Malik Awais and Maulana Amjad Khan were detained at a house in Sargodha and served notices for violating Section 144 imposed across the division.

He added that several other party leaders had also been arrested.

Responding to a question about Maulana Haideri’s arrest, Sukhera said the leaders had not been arrested but that “their movement had been restricted in the division”.

In a post on X last night, JUI-F claimed that Punjab police had “arrested” MNA Haideri, Maulana Khan and Awais.

“The government should come to its senses; if they are not released immediately, the Punjab government will be held responsible for the consequences,” the post quoted party spokesperson Aslam Ghouri as saying.

He questioned why political gatherings were banned when Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz herself was holding rallies.

“Do opposition parties not have the right to hold such gatherings?” he asked.

“Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri is a member of the National Assembly; was his arrest carried out with the permission of the NA Speaker?” the spokesperson said.

Ghouri demanded the immediate release of the leaders, adding that “arrests made without warrants were a slap in the face of democracy”.

He further maintained that homes of JUI-F office bearers were being raided.

Leaders detained under MPO in Khushab

Meanwhile, several local JUI-F leaders were detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Punjab’s Khushab district late on Wednesday, police said.

A first information report (FIR), a copy of which is available with Dawn, was registered under Sections 188 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant), 290 (punishment for public nuisance), 341 (punishment for wrongful restraint), 147 (punishment for rioting) and 149 (every member of an unlawful assembly guilty of an offence committed in prosecution of a common object) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Section 16 (dissemination of rumours) of the MPO.

The FIR named Maulana Abdullah Ahmed, Qazi Umair Ahmed, Muhammad Abdur Rehman Saud, Muhammad Dilawar Khan, Muhammad Ammar, Hasnain Muawiya, Muhammad Ismail Khan, Muhammad Umar, Ibrahim Khan, Muhammad Qasim Afzal and Muhammad Awais Ahmed. It also mentioned nine to 10 unidentified individuals who were carrying sticks and managed to flee. The named individuals were reportedly carrying JUI-F flags.

According to the FIR, police officials were patrolling Purana Chowk in Khushab to inspect security arrangements when they found Maulana Abdullah Ahmed violating Section 144 by gathering people for a rally outside Madrasa Taleem-ul-Islam and “inciting them through inflammatory speeches”.

Following this, the police immediately conducted a raid.

“A large number of people gathered outside the Madrasa, blocking the street and public thoroughfare,” it stated, adding that they were brought under control.

It stated that the Khushab deputy commissioner had imposed a complete ban on gatherings, rallies, processions and protests under Section 144 on November 23. The nominated individuals had violated the order and “incited the crowd by delivering inflammatory speeches”.

Fazl-govt rift

On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

The JUI-F chief was scheduled to participate in a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association on Tuesday. However, he could not leave his residence in a private housing society on Multan Road due to the deployment of a heavy police contingent.

The development came after tensions persisted between JUI-F and the Centre. Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks.

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

JUI-F spokesman Ghouri had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz launches ‘Mehfooz Dawa’ app to combat counterfeit and substandard medicines
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday launched the “Mehfooz Dawa” app to prevent the circulation of counterfeit and substandard medicines, calling it “a major milestone” and saying the initiative would help restore public confidence in the healthcare system.

The prime minister said education and healthcare facilities should be equally accessible to every citizen and stressed that the federal and provincial governments must work together to ensure the availability of affordable, quality medicines.

The prime minister was speaking at the launch ceremony of the Ministry of National Health Services’ “Mehfooz Dawa” app, which was developed to track medicines.

Federal Minister for National Health Services Mustafa Kamal and Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) Chief Executive Officer Dr Obaidullah also addressed the event.

Addressing the ceremony, PM Shehbaz hailed the development, describing it as “an extremely magnificent moment” for Pakistan’s medical facilities.

He recalled a 2012 incident at the Punjab Institute of Cardiology in which counterfeit medication was blamed for the deaths of more than 100 patients. At the time, DRAP had maintained that the medication was genuine; however, international testing found that the medicine administered to the patients was intended to treat malaria.

He called for “learning from the past and preparing ourselves” for the future. The prime minister lauded Kamal’s efforts and directed his ministry to work with the IT and Information ministries to raise public awareness about the app.

“History will remember this step in golden words,” the premier remarked.

Noting the application’s mechanism, the premier said it was an “excellent intervention”.

“But the real point is that, to make medicines affordable for the common man, their prices should be in line with what ordinary people can afford,” he said, stressing that obtaining medicines was a “huge challenge” for millions of people in the country.

The prime minister further said: “The founding principle of our policies should be that health and education are equal for everyone and no one should have to go begging and pleading at anyone’s door.”

Speaking at the ceremony, the health minister said the application had been developed with the aim of “protecting innocent lives”. He also noted a “lack of trust” among the public when it came to obtaining medicines.

He praised the pharmaceutical industry’s cooperation, adding that building a database covering around 92,000 medicines and involving more than 700 companies had been an “uphill task”.

Dr Obaidullah explained that the app sought to address three issues: counterfeit medicines, shortages and quality compliance.

The application has three features — medicine verification, complaints and shortage reporting, he said.

By scanning a medicine’s batch number, which would then be checked against a database, users can verify whether the product is authentic, he said. The application will display a green screen if the medicine is genuine and a red screen if it is counterfeit.

If a medicine is found to be counterfeit, consumers will have the option to lodge a complaint. He added that DRAP’s database, which is linked to the application, contains details of around 92,000 medicines.

Users will also be able to report medicine shortages through the application, the DRAP chief said. He added that the government had provided citizens with “protected public health” through the application.

Earlier this month, Drap’s spokesperson Sajid Shah had said the track-and-trace system became operational on October 9.

The idea of introducing a barcode system was first proposed in 2015. It was approved by the federal cabinet in 2017; however, bureaucratic delays prevented its implementation.

Earlier, Kamal, taking notice of the delay, announced that the system would be launched as soon as possible.

Earlier this year, Drap had set October 1 as the cut-off date for launching the barcode system to curb the sale of counterfeit and expired medicines and eradicate black marketing.

Shah said the Ministry of National Health Services was “dedicated” to ensuring that citizens had access to high-quality and effective therapeutic products.

articles.title: US clears SpaceX to launch up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites
articles.summary:
The Trump administration authorised Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Wednesday to launch up to one million satellites as part of its plan to build data centres in space, raising concerns from some experts.

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said SpaceX’s Starmind constellation would “process massive amounts of data to be used back here on Earth.”

The company’s authorisation runs until 2040, according to a document published on the FCC’s website.

“America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement, using Trump’s moniker for artificial intelligence.

He added that data centres would be “essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI.” Projects for orbiting data centres have multiplied over the past year.

Alongside SpaceX and its Starmind constellation, Google is pursuing its own initiative under the codename “Suncatcher,” while Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin has submitted an application to the FCC for its “Project Sunrise.”

Several startups are also in the race, including Starcloud, which successfully operated an advanced processor known as a GPU aboard a satellite in late 2025. Google also reached that milestone in October.

SpaceX has the advantage of having its own rockets that have already completed hundreds of missions.

In August, Musk promised a first SpaceX satellite launch into orbit in the fourth quarter of 2027 and a ramp-up in 2028.

The company has struck a deal with Nvidia, which will supply its latest-generation Vera Rubin processors, specially designed to operate in space.

‘Disheartened and dismayed’

Most space-based data centre projects have a similar architecture: a constellation of satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO), positioned close together to ensure reliable connections between them.

Starmind’s satellites will communicate with those already in orbit as part of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet network, which will then relay the data to Earth.

Other competing networks plan to receive data directly from Earth and send it back using lasers.

But experts have warned of technical obstacles, as well as environmental concerns.

Unresolved technical challenges include processors’ ability to withstand the high levels of radiation in space.

Observers also point to the difficulty of withstanding extreme temperatures or avoiding damage from space debris and micrometeorites.

The American Astronomical Society (AAS) said it was “disheartened and dismayed” by Wednesday’s decision.

“The proposed constellation would significantly undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities and the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky,” the AAS said in a statement.

It noted that the constellation “involves larger (and therefore brighter) and more numerous objects,” meaning the satellites would “be visible as extremely bright objects for longer periods in the night sky.”

“Drastically expanding satellites in space has a direct impact on people’s everyday lives as well as the future of our planet,” Jan Hasselman, a senior attorney at the nonprofit group Earthjustice, said in a statement.

However, there are numerous advantages to locating a data centre in space over building one on Earth.

Among those, a satellite in what is known as a sun-synchronous orbit can capture solar energy continuously and with eight times the efficiency of its ground-based equivalent.

SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion.

articles.title: Major economies balk at new US tariffs over 'unfair' trade
articles.summary:
Major economies from China to the European Union hit out at proposed US tariffs after Washington concluded its months-long probe into alleged excess production, potentially opening a new phase in trade tensions with both allies and foes alike.

The new tolls, which follow an investigation launched days after the Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s previous duties, range up to 20 per cent and face a period of public comment before taking effect, at the earliest in January.

The levies target some of the United States’ largest trading partners, with China, the EU, India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam in the crosshairs.

A senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, noted that the proposals sought to take existing trade deals into account.

China is among those facing a 20 per cent tariff, but US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the levies were within the bounds of existing trade negotiations with Beijing.

“China understands that we’re going to have some level of tariffs. This falls within that understanding,” he told US broadcaster CNBC, adding that Washington was offering China exemptions on around $30 billion of goods.

Beijing hit out at the proposed tariffs on Thursday, warning that it could take “necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests.”

Chinese commerce ministry spokesman He Yadong told a regular briefing that citing “overcapacity” — mass production at a loss to flood overseas markets and undercut local rivals — as a reason to impose tariffs was a “pretext for protectionism.”

He urged Washington “to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation.”

‘Real concern’

Along with other countries, Japan denied having excessive production.

“Japan does not have any non-market policy practices or structural excess production capacity … It is regrettable that a proposed measure targeting Japan has been announced in spite of this,” top government spokesman Minoru Kihara said.

The EU said it rejected the premise of the new tariffs and expected the United States to stick by a deal struck last year.

“The EU and the US share a real concern about global overcapacity, much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action,” European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said.

And Singapore said it was “very disappointed” with the proposals, and denied it was protecting its domestic market or subsidising manufacturing.

Vietnam also faces a 20pc tariff; Cambodia and Indonesia 18pc; and India 17pc, according to the US trade representative’s office.

The EU, South Korea and Taiwan, which have signed trade deals with the United States, will see tariffs broadly capped at 15pc.

In a separate announcement, the trade representative also proposed additional tariffs on goods from Brazil, including aircraft, over alleged inaction on addressing US trade concerns.

The Brazilian president’s office called the measures “unacceptable” and said Brasilia would “not yield to this type of threat”.

Trump’s tariffs have targeted Washington’s friends and foes alike, and are part of a push in his second term to remake global trade by forcing countries to buy US products or produce their goods in the country.

Overcapacity concerns affect a range of sectors, from batteries to cement and chemicals to processed food, the senior US official said.

‘Hollowing out’

The duties could add further pressure on US businesses already squeezed by earlier tariffs, with firms now more likely to pass on expenses to consumers already frustrated with the high cost of living.

Affordability was a key issue in this month’s US midterm elections, which saw Trump’s Republican Party swept out of power in both chambers of Congress by Democrats.

The announcement came as data showed the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge at a three-year high in October, adding to pressure to hike interest rates.

Trade lawyer Ryan Majerus told AFP that he expected the production probe to be among “the most important” actions for the Trump administration, given its underlying concern that factories with excess capacity start operations abroad and “never get turned off, even if there’s no demand.”

This could potentially lead to an oversupply of goods, depressed prices and a “hollowing out” of US manufacturing, he added.

While the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s global tariffs in February, his sector-specific duties remain intact.

The new levies will not stack on top of those sector-specific tariffs on items like automobiles and steel, the senior US official said.

In July, Trump imposed a separate wave of tariffs on 60 economies, accusing them of insufficient action against forced labour.

For economies facing both the forced labour and excess production tariffs, the levies would not stack up and the higher rate would prevail, the US official said.

articles.title: ‘To the moon and beyond’: PM says Shenzhou-24 mission ‘living proof’ of Pak-China friendship
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday described the Shenzhou-24 mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister made the remarks during a meeting with Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, who called on him at the Prime Minister House.

On Wednesday, Wing Comm­ander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic milestone in Pakistan’s space ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to expand its space diplomacy.

The first Pakistani to travel into orbit, part of the three-member crew of the Shenzhou-24 mission, is serving as a payload specialist and is expected to remain at the station for five to 10 days.

On Thursday, PM Shehbaz met the Chinese envoy and congratulated him and China’s people and leadership on the successful launch.

The prime minister highlighted that Pakistan was “grateful” to China for the opportunity to be part of this historic mission, through which a Pakistani had become the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s space station, the statement said.

“The prime minister said that this was not merely the journey of an individual astronaut, but that of 240 million Pakistanis, embodying, in particular, the dreams and aspirations of the country’s youth and scientific community,” the statement said.

He described the mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, adding that cooperation between the two countries had now “truly reached the stars”.

The prime minister expressed his appreciation to the relevant Chinese institutions for training Pakistani astronauts and paid tribute to Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco), academic institutions, scientists and the armed forces for their contributions to this historic achievement.

He said that the achievement would inspire Pakistan’s youth to “aim for the moon and beyond”.

The prime minister requested the ambassador to convey his warm greetings and best wishes to President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang.

“He paid rich tribute to the dynamic leadership and sagacious vision of President Xi, under which China has made remarkable strides in science, technology and space exploration and has opened its space programme to friendly countries for the benefit of humanity,” the statement said.

He underlined that Pakistan remained unwavering in its commitment to work hand in hand with China for the peaceful exploration and utilisation of outer space, it added.

The two sides also reviewed bilateral relations, including activities organised to commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year. PM Shehbaz also handed over congratulatory letters addressed to President Xi and Premier Li to the Chinese ambassador, the statement concluded.

articles.title: IHC extends stay on Islamabad LG polls for two weeks
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday extended its interim order suspending local government elections in the federal capital by another two weeks and sought para-wise comments from the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP).

Justice Umair Majeed Malik was hearing petitions challenging the delimitation of constituencies for Islamabad’s local government elections.

During the hearing, Barrister Adil Aziz Qazi appeared on behalf of the petitioners. The ECP’s counsel informed the court that the commission had suspended the election schedule following the court’s stay order.

Justice Malik observed that the issue of delimitation had not been resolved, questioning how elections could be held when, according to the petitioners, a particular ward had only two voters.

The judge asked the ECP officials to explain whether the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the 2015 law.

The ECP’s counsel submitted that the commission had issued a detailed order explaining the reasons behind its decision. He said the commission had conducted the delimitation exercise six times in accordance with the relevant law.

The court observed that if the commission had initiated proper proceedings, an appeal could have been filed against its decision. It also questioned whether the ECP could still alter the delimitations after issuing the election schedule.

Justice Malik remarked that the commission would have to satisfy the court that the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the law. He noted that several petitions had previously been filed over the matter.

The judge also observed that the petitioners claimed they did not even know which wards they belonged to.

The ECP’s counsel maintained that the commission had carried out the delimitation exercise in accordance with the applicable law and issued an order on October 14 declaring the process complete.

The court sought a detailed response from the ECP and adjourned the proceedings for two weeks.

Two weeks ago, Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad.

The local government elections in Islamabad have faced numerous delays and postponements since the term of the last local government expired in February 2021.

The ECP has issued multiple schedules, only to cancel them later for various reasons, including legislative changes and court orders. The delimitation of constituencies and union councils was carried out six times, while the election schedule was issued four times.

The ECP had decided that, since the local government law enacted in 2015 was still in force, elections would be held under the Act. This meant polls would be held in 50 constituencies, after which the mayor and deputy mayors would be elected.

After the completion of various stages of the electoral process, it had decided that polling would be held on Dec 20. The ECP had reserved four days, from December 21 to 24, for the consolidation of results.

articles.title: Rawalpindi ATC defers verdict in November 2024 protest case involving Aleema Khan until Dec 16
articles.summary:
RAWALPINDI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Rawalpindi on Thursday adjourned until December 16 the announcement of its reserved verdict in a case registered against Aleema Khan, sister of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, in connection with the November 26, 2024 protest.

ATC Judge Amjad Ali Shah deferred the verdict for the sixth time without holding any further proceedings.

Aleema’s counsel, Faisal Malik, appeared before the court on Thursday.

The court had reserved its verdict in the case on September 22, fixing Sept 25 as the announcement date. However, the announcement was deferred after Judge Shah went on leave, with October 1 set as the next date.

The verdict has since been postponed several times, with the latest adjournment pushing it to Dec 16.

Aleema’s counsel had also objected to the court reserving its verdict without hearing the defence’s arguments, saying he had not been given an opportunity to present his case.

In September, Aleema was detained under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance ahead of a PTI march towards Islamabad. She remains incarcerated at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail.

The case

The case came to be known as the November 26 protest case. The protest saw more than 10,000 PTI supporters enter Islamabad in 2024, defying a ban on public gatherings and a lockdown, and clash with around 20,000 security personnel deployed to prevent them from advancing.

A day of clashes between security forces and protesters in the city’s Red Zone ended with the PTI leadership retreating, after which the party announced that it was calling off its planned protest sit-in “for the time being”.

Subsequently, cases were registered against several PTI leaders under various sections of the Pakistan Penal Code and Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act. Two of the cases were registered at Taxila police station and one each at Sadiqabad and Naseerabad police stations.

Aleema, along with 10 others, was booked in the case registered at Sadiqabad police station.

articles.title: Egypt says 31 dead in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns
articles.summary:
A fire erupted in Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday killing at least 31 people, the health ministry said, after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway.

AFP footage showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists sounded their horns and scrambled to get away. Surrounding buildings appeared to escape the flames.

State media reported that the fire broke out when a truck loaded with fuel overturned on Cairo’s Ring Road — a crowded highway linking different parts of the capital — and burst into flames, engulfing nearby vehicles.

The health ministry said 39 ambulances were sent to the scene and 15 people were taken to hospital with injuries, four of them in critical condition.

“The scene was terrifying,” Abdel Rahman Khalil told AFP, saying he arrived shortly after the crash and saw the overturned fuel truck engulfed in flames.

AFP images showed a grisly aftermath with cars burned out, as firefighters doused the truck’s wreckage.

Egypt’s public prosecutor said an investigation had been opened and DNA tests were being carried out to identify badly burned victims.

The health ministry said it had raised its emergency alert level and Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar had travelled to the scene and nearby hospitals.

Charred wreckage

The health minister’s spokesman told state-linked Al-Qahera News that “the Ring Road has been reopened, and the remnants of the accident have been cleared.”

Footage carried by Al-Qahera News showed the charred truck’s wreckage being removed, while traffic partially resumed around it.

A spokesperson for the Egyptian Cabinet told local media that Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly had ordered an investigation into the causes of the accident.

He said the government was awaiting a full clarification before determining “future measures regarding the transport of petroleum products and ensuring safety and security during such transport operations”.

Road deaths

Egypt, with its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, has suffered several deadly fires in recent years.

Fire escapes, smoke detectors and alarms are rare and in many areas, warrens of narrow roads make it hard for fire engines to reach disaster sites.

Car crashes are also common, and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted.

Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency.

The year before, more than 5,200 road deaths were recorded across the country, according to authorities.

In August, at least 18 people, many of them teenagers, were killed in northern Egypt when two pick-up trucks carrying agricultural day-labourers crashed.

PM, DPM express condolences

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said he was “deeply grieved by the tragic loss of precious lives”.

In a post on X, he wrote, “On behalf of the people and Government of Pakistan, I extend my heartfelt condolences to President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, the bereaved families and the brotherly people of Egypt.”

Reaffirming Pakistan’s solidarity with Egypt in the hour of grief, he said his thoughts and prayers were with those who had lost their loved ones.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in a post on X, also expressed his condolences for the loss of lives in Cairo.

“Deeply saddened by the tragic loss of precious lives in the fuel tanker fire near Cairo.

“I extend my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and the Government and brotherly people of Egypt,” he wrote.

He added, “Pakistan stands in solidarity with Egypt during this difficult time.”

articles.title: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR
articles.summary:
Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces targeted a terrorist hideout in Nushki district on November 20. Following an intense exchange of fire, eight terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the site, the ISPR added.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

On November 21, security forces intercepted the movement of terrorists in Sibi district, killing two more, the ISPR said.

In two separate engagements in Panjgur and Kech districts on November 22 and 23, security forces raided terrorist hideouts and killed two more terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan, the ISPR added.

The ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-i-Istehkam”, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace to eliminate the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

Meanwhile, President Asif Ali Zardari lauded the security forces for carrying out “successful intelligence-based operations” in Balochistan against “terrorists operating under India’s patronage”, a statement issued by his office said.

The statement quoted him as saying: “Security forces’ continued successes in the fight against terrorism demonstrate their commitment and sacrifices for peace and stability in the country.”

He added that the “elimination of Fitna-al-Hindustan and foreign-backed terrorists is essential for national security. Security forces and law enforcement agencies will continue operations against foreign-backed and -supported terrorists in every part of Pakistan”.

Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. Last week, 15 terrorists were killed during two separate operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district.

On Nov 14, four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple IBOs in Balochistan and KP.

On Nov 1, a soldier was martyred while 17 terrorists were killed in two IBOs in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts.

According to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, Pakistan recorded fewer terrorist attacks from Nov 6 to 12, but fatalities and injuries increased sharply, “highlighting the changing intensity and continued volatility of militant threat across the country”.

KP remained the principal centre of violence, accounting for 16 attacks and 44 fatalities. Balochistan recorded 13 attacks, resulting in eight deaths and 19 injuries, while the former tribal districts witnessed a “substantial” reduction in attacks.

articles.title: 2027: Uba Sani tells Northern leaders to prepare for 2031 presidency
articles.summary:
Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has urged political leaders in Northern Nigeria to put aside demands for the presidency in 2027 and begin preparations for the region’s possible return to power in 2031.

The governor said the North should use the next four years to develop a comprehensive governance blueprint capable of addressing its developmental challenges and preparing the region for future leadership.

Sani made the remarks on Thursday at an endorsement programme organised by the Arewa Think Tank and civil society groups in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections.

He argued that Northern politicians needed to examine their readiness for national leadership rather than rely on regional sentiments and demands for power.

According to him, the region currently lacks a clear development plan that could serve as a foundation for its next presidential ambition.

“I told them, show me the blueprint. We need to start working for a blueprint today so that in 2031, when we want the power to pass back to the North, we are set to implement. But today, we are not ready yet because there is no blueprint as we are speaking,” he said.

The governor also cautioned against seeking electoral support solely on the basis of ethnic or regional identity, insisting that political candidates should be judged by their records in public office.

He questioned the rationale behind politicians asking Nigerians to vote for them simply because they were from the North.

“Someone said, ‘Vote for me because I am a northerner.’ Does it make sense? No!” he asked.

Sani maintained that politicians should present verifiable achievements rather than make promises without evidence of previous performance.

“The era of promises is over. It is over. We are urging politicians: don’t come with promises, please,” he stated.

He challenged former governors, vice-presidents and other public office holders seeking political positions to account for their contributions to their respective states, regions and the country.

The Kaduna governor further called on Northern leaders to concentrate on education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture and economic empowerment as part of efforts to address the region’s challenges.

He also advocated regional cooperation, constructive engagement and evidence-based planning, urging political stakeholders to move beyond highlighting problems and develop practical solutions.

Explaining his support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition, Sani pointed to federal government projects and intervention programmes in Kaduna State and other parts of the North.

He cited road construction, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), the Technical and Vocational Education and Training programme and other social intervention initiatives.

The governor specifically commended Tinubu for approving the Mando-Birnin Gwari road project in Kaduna, which he said had received N178 billion in federal government funding.

According to Sani, the project followed decades of demands by residents and a commitment made by Tinubu during a campaign visit to Birnin Gwari on December 27, 2022.

He also disclosed that the President had approved the Zaria-Soba-Pambegua and Jama’a-Kwai road projects following requests from his administration.

On transportation, Sani said his government had deployed 100 compressed natural gas buses to provide free transportation for residents.

He disclosed that the initiative had recorded 5.2 million passenger trips and saved beneficiaries more than N5 billion.

The governor also announced plans to commission a modern bus terminal in Kaduna with a capacity for 5,000 buses, alongside another facility in Kafanchan designed to accommodate about 500 vehicles.

Sani reiterated that his endorsement of Tinubu was based on what he described as the President’s contributions to Kaduna State and Northern Nigeria.

articles.title: 20 years ago with Muammar Ghaddafi
articles.summary:
By Amb Olufemi Fani-Kayode

Permit me to take you on an interesting journey of historical discovery.

On November 26, 2006, which is 20 years ago to the day, the great leader Muammar Ghaddafi of Libya came to Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit.

As Minister of Aviation at the time, I had the honour and privilege of receiving him at the airport on behalf of my boss, His Excellency President Olusegun Obasanjo, and I was detailed to spend the next four days with him, accompanying him wherever he went.

There is no doubt that Ghaddafi’s charisma was infectious and, after spending those four days with him, my perception of him changed from that of a wary sceptic to one of his most vocal admirers.

He was a truly extraordinary man who really did love Africa.

Yet his visit had a very bumpy start.

He arrived at the airport with no fewer than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja.

The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons.

They took them from one of the three planes he came in and loaded the boots of the cars with them.

We then proceeded to leave the airport in convoy, but we were blocked at the gate by our security personnel and our military.

We were told that it was because of the weapons and that, whilst Ghaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in (with their sidearms), the high-powered weapons that were in the boots of their vehicles would not.

I was in the car with Ghaddafi and I had the onerous task of explaining the situation to him through his interpreter, who was in the car with us.

We went back to the airport and tried to leave again three times, but we were blocked each time and, during the course of each attempt, tempers were rising.

The next thing that happened was beyond shocking.

Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja, saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!

I was right next to him, in panic mode, as we walked, and my fear was that he would collapse under the sun as a consequence of walking so far.

What made my fear even more acute and pronounced was that he was already sweating profusely and panting.

I was expecting the worst even as I was appealing to him not to do this.

My appeals fell on deaf ears.

I called President Obasanjo and, luckily for us all, he told me that he was on his way to the airport to catch a flight and attend a function in Lagos.

He said I should tell Ghaddafi that he was on his way to the airport to settle the matter himself and get him to go back to the airport, which I did.

Luckily, Ghaddafi, after being told that OBJ was on his way, agreed to do so, especially after I said that he was rushing to the airport to address the matter himself and appeal to him.

When OBJ arrived, they greeted and hugged one another warmly and, after a very brief conversation, OBJ got up to leave and told him that he was off to Lagos and would be back later in the day and in time for the opening session of the conference the following morning.

As he was leaving, Ghaddafi told him that there was an issue at the gate and that he had been blocked three times.

OBJ feigned ignorance of the event, apologised to him profusely and said the gates would be opened for him immediately.

However, as he walked past me, he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK-47s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane.

After that, he disappeared and left me to handle the mess.

I told Ghaddafi that the weapons needed to be removed and his men reluctantly complied after I had a hot encounter and harsh exchange of words with his Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol, who were very rude to our security officers, our military personnel and our officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs who were present, and who had threatened to fly Ghaddafi back to Libya there and then and boycott the entire conference if we refused to allow them to take their heavy weapons in.

The weapons were taken out of the boots of the cars and loaded back onto the plane, after which a contingent of our soldiers surrounded the plane in order to ensure that they were not smuggled out later.

We then proceeded to the gate and the convoy was allowed through.

As we were leaving, my wife Regina called me on the phone and said the whole matter was being reported in detail on the BBC and that she hoped all was well.

I assured her that the matter had been amicably resolved and that we were on our way to town.

On his part, Ghaddafi, still angry, remained silent in the car throughout our ride into Abuja, and the only time he spoke was when we drove past the Central Mosque and he said how beautiful it was.

It was that day that I learnt about the intricacies of diplomacy and the fact that firmness, the display of mutual respect and strict adherence to the rules of engagement were vital.

On that day, our military personnel and security agencies, who were determined to implement the directives from the President and their commanders, made me proud, whilst the wisdom, strength and courage that OBJ displayed were instructive and exemplary.

We stood our ground and had our way and, because we did so, Ghaddafi and his team showed us massive respect from that moment on.

For the next four days, during the course of the conference, he and I became very close and he even invited me as his personal guest to Libya.

The only complaint he had was that I had worn a suit for each of those days and that he would have preferred me to wear an agbada or babariga!

I told him that that is precisely what my wife had said!

The whole experience was surreal.

Ghaddafi was a truly extraordinary and inspiring man and, as I studied him closely for those four days, I learnt much from him.

As for my boss OBJ, he saved lives on that day by putting his foot down and insisting that the heavy weapons must not be let in because, as I was later told when the matter was discussed at the next cabinet meeting, what the Libyans had done in the past when they carried in such weapons was to hand them over to their local associates and leave them behind.

Those lethal weapons would later become part of a stockpile of arms that provided a massive arsenal for terrorists, insurgents and other ruthless non-state actors within our country.

On October 20th 2011, five years almost to the day and month after his visit to our country and our extraordinary airport encounter, Muammar Ghaddafi met a violent end at the hands of his own people in his home town, Sirte.

I watched the footage of his brutal murder on CNN and was deeply saddened.

No one deserves to be killed in such a barbaric manner.

That an all-powerful leader who was literally worshipped by his people could come to such a bloody end in the flash of an eye spoke volumes and serves as a lesson to us all.

This was a clear and graphic example and confirmation of the ephemeral and transient nature of power and the futility of the vanity that goes with it.

What hit me even more was the fact that the Head of Protocol, who spoke so loudly and aggressively on the day of our encounter and who said that if we did not allow the arms to be taken in they would fly Ghaddafi back home, was one of those condemning him on CNN all the way from Paris on the day he was murdered.

Such is life!

_____________________________________________

Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode is Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, a former Minister of Culture and Tourism and a former Minister of Aviation

The post 20 years ago with Muammar Ghaddafi appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Crypto Loan Accounts: What Happens to Personal Data After Closure
articles.summary:
An account closure message may say little about the passport scan submitted during registration or the messages sent to support. Those records can remain in storage after access to the account has ended.

A person sees one profile, but the company may hold several kinds of information about them. The email address used for notifications serves a different purpose from a document collected to check identity. They may have different deletion schedules too.

More than a registration form

When someone creates an account to borrow crypto, the first request may be for basic contact details. Later checks can involve a photograph or an identity document. The company may also record device information and login activity.

A crypto backed loan application can add another set of records. From the user’s point of view, all these details belong to the same account. Inside the company, they may be kept in separate systems, with access limited to the teams responsible for each task.

Support messages create a further complication. A conversation about a crypto collateral loan application might include personal information already supplied elsewhere. Removing one copy would not necessarily remove the details from that conversation.

Under the GDPR, where it applies, companies need a lawful basis for processing personal data. Consent is one possibility. A contract or a legal obligation may provide another basis, so withdrawing consent does not automatically end every use of the information.

Who holds the records

The company running the crypto loan website may use an outside provider for identity checks. Document images or verification results can then pass through another organisation, even though the user completes the process through one interface.

European data protection rules distinguish between the controller, which decides why and how information is processed, and a processor working on its behalf. The roles depend on the arrangement between the organisations. An outside provider is not automatically a processor in every situation.

For a cryptocurrency loan service, the privacy notice explains who is responsible for personal information and describes the purposes of processing. It also covers recipients or categories of recipients and how long information is kept, or the criteria used to decide that period.

An “instant crypto loan” label offers no answer to those questions. It describes the product, while storage periods belong to the company’s data practices.

Account closure brings those practices into focus. Under the GDPR, a person can request erasure in certain circumstances, but exceptions allow records to remain when needed for a legal obligation or legal claims.

That leaves a practical difference between a closed profile and deleted information. A closure confirmation concerns the account. A response to an erasure request addresses the personal data, including whether any records must remain and why.

articles.title: Plateau attack: death toll rises to 19
articles.summary:
. Victims get mass burial

____________________________________________________________________

From Jude Owuamanam, Jos

Three more people have died from the attack on Tafi-Gana, a community in Jebbu Miango, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, bringing the death toll to 19.

Seventeen of the victims were said to have been given a mass burial on Thursday.

Initial reports had put the death toll at 16 in the attack, which occurred on Wednesday night and continued into the early hours of Thursday.

A resident of the community, Moses Monday, who confirmed the casualty figure on Thursday, said 16 bodies were recovered at the scene, while three other victims died after they were taken to hospital.

Monday said: “I can confirm that 16 bodies have so far been recovered at the spot, with an additional three who died after they were taken to the hospital. These evil men will not rest.”

Another resident, Nuhu Fidelis, who confirmed the new figure, described it as another assault on the neighbouring community in Jebbu Miango.

Fidelis said: “Yes, in the early morning of today, Thursday. Last night, November 25, 2026, a Christian neighbouring village, Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), in Jebbu Miango, Bassa LGA, Plateau State, was attacked again. Many innocent people lost their lives.”

While condemning the killings, he called on the government and security agencies to take urgent measures to protect the people.

Paul Nehemiah, another resident, who said he lost a close relative in the attack, described it as wicked, adding that the unprovoked attack had left residents apprehensive and living in fear.

Nehemiah said: “We are tired of burying our people. These are farmers, women and children who did nothing to anyone. How long will this continue? We are calling on the government to rise up and save us.”

Another resident, Rita Joseph, whose family fled into the bush during the attack, said community members could no longer sleep peacefully because of the persistent security threats.

The residents appealed to the Plateau State Government, the Federal Government and security agencies to deploy more personnel to Miango and surrounding communities to prevent further attacks.

Meanwhile, 17 of the people killed in an attack on Tafi Gana community in Irigwe Chiefdom, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, were given a mass burial on Thursday amid grief and calls for justice.

The National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Yonkpa, confirmed the mass burial in a statement.

According to him, the victims were killed when more than 200 armed men attacked the community at about 11pm on Wednesday night.

articles.title: CBN appoints Murtala Mohammed to head Keystone Bank
articles.summary:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has appointed Murtala Mohammed as Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Keystone Bank Limited, replacing Hassan Imam with effect from November 26, 2026.

The appointment was announced in a statement issued by the CBN on Thursday and signed by its Director of Corporate Communications and Investor Relations, Michael Akuka.

The apex bank said the appointment was made under the powers granted to it by the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA) 2020, which empowers it to regulate banks and take necessary steps to protect the stability of the financial system.

Although the CBN did not disclose the circumstances surrounding Imam’s exit or give details of Mohammed’s previous positions and banking experience, it said the decision was in line with its responsibility to ensure a safe, sound and stable banking industry.

The regulator also moved to reassure customers and depositors that the leadership change would not disrupt the bank’s operations.

According to the statement, Keystone Bank remains fully operational, with banking services continuing as normal and customers’ deposits secure.

“The CBN remains committed to safeguarding depositors’ interests and ensuring the continued soundness and stability of Nigeria’s banking sector,” the statement said.

The latest appointment comes against the background of previous regulatory interventions in the bank.

Keystone Bank was established on August 5, 2011, after the CBN revoked the operating licence of Bank PHB over its financial difficulties.

The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) transferred Bank PHB’s assets and deposit liabilities to the newly established Keystone Bank to protect depositors and ensure uninterrupted banking services.

The Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON) subsequently took over the bank before selling it in March 2017 to the Sigma Golf-Riverbank Consortium, comprising Sigma Golf Nigeria Limited and Riverbank Investment Resources Limited.

However, the bank experienced another major ownership and management shake-up in recent years.

On January 10, 2024, the CBN dissolved its board and management over alleged corporate governance breaches and appointed a new leadership team.

In another development, a Lagos State Special Offences Court ordered the forfeiture of the bank’s shares previously held by its former shareholders to the Federal Government in February 2025.

Keystone Bank subsequently announced that the development made it fully owned by the Federal Government.

The CBN’s latest appointment of Mohammed, therefore, represents another change in the leadership of the lender, although the regulator has not linked the decision to any fresh governance breach or financial difficulty.

The CBN supervises banks to ensure they operate within regulatory requirements, protect depositors and maintain confidence in the financial system.

articles.title: Ogun police rescue stolen child abducted at 11 months, arrest three suspects
articles.summary:
The Ogun State Command has rescued a boy who was allegedly abducted at 11 months old from his mother at Ifo Market, Ogun State, on August 26.

In a Thursday statement, the command spokesman, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi said operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit and detectives of Ifo Divisional Police Headquarters rescued the victim.

He added that the child, now one year old, has been successfully rescued and reunited with his mother, while three female suspects have been arrested in connection with the incident.

He said detectives commenced preliminary investigations following a report lodged at Ifo Divisional Police Headquarters, before the case was referred to the Anti-Kidnapping Unit.

Working collaboratively, both teams pursued intelligence leads that culminated in the arrest of Opeyemi Imoleayo Oni, aged 37, on October 20.

During investigation, she allegedly confessed to taking the child under the pretext of offering financial assistance to his mother through the establishment of a wig business.

She further disclosed that she had allegedly sold the child to one Obi Ifunanya, aged 54, for N1.5 million.

Further investigation led to Ifunanya’s arrest on November 11, 2026.

She allegedly disclosed that she had subsequently resold the child to one Loveth Moses, who is currently at large, for N1.8 million.

Sustained investigative efforts by the joint team led to the arrest of another suspect, Lian Musa, aged 30, at Abule Egba, Lagos State, on November 20.

In a further breakthrough, Musa led the joint team of detectives to the Iyana Mortuary area of Abeokuta, Ogun State, where the child was recovered from a couple who had allegedly been deceived into believing that the child was being offered for adoption through an orphanage in Lagos State.

The police said the circumstances surrounding the child’s transfer to the couple were being investigated.

The child has since been safely reunited with his mother.

Meanwhile, the joint investigative team has intensified efforts to apprehend Loveth Moses and other persons suspected to be connected with the incident.

Babaseyi said investigation continues to establish the respective roles of all persons involved and unravel the full circumstances surrounding the alleged abduction and trafficking.

The Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, CP Bode Ojajuni, commended the operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit and detectives of Ifo Division for their coordinated efforts, diligence and persistence, which culminated in the successful recovery of the child.

He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting children and combating kidnapping, child trafficking and related offences.

He urged parents and guardians to remain vigilant against suspicious offers and approaches involving their children, assuring residents that the command would continue to pursue all persons connected with such criminal activities and ensure that anyone found culpable is brought to justice in accordance with the law.

articles.title: China-Africa Youth Festival: China stands ready to continue working with Africa – Foreign Ministry
articles.summary:
From Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja

The Chinese Foreign Ministry has said that China stands ready to continue working with African countries to promote mutual learning and exchanges, and to deepen mutual understanding and friendship.

The spokesperson of the Chinese Foreign Ministry, Guo Jiakun, speaking during a press conference in Beijing, also said the Chinese government is ready to advance the respective modernisation drives of both sides and, together, build a community with a shared future for humanity.

Guo was responding to the outcome of the 10th China-Africa Youth Festival, which took place in Beijing and Shaanxi.

He explained that the China-Africa Youth Festival is a regular event under the framework of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

He added that ten consecutive editions have taken place so far and that the event is widely popular among young people from both China and Africa.

The Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson further said that the 10th festival was recently held successfully in Beijing and Shaanxi, where more than 60 African youths visited the Museum of the Communist Party of China and the Yan’an Revolutionary Memorial Hall to learn about the party’s great journey.

The youths, he stated, also visited the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, where they learned about China’s socialist consultative democracy.

“They also explored the rich heritage of the Chinese civilization at the Palace Museum, and visited high-tech companies to gain first-hand insight into the dynamism of China’s economy. Through a wide range of engaging activities, young people from both sides had in-depth and heartfelt exchanges, further strengthening their bonds of friendship.

“This year marks the 70th anniversary of the establishment of China-Africa diplomatic relations and the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges. China stands ready to continue working with the African side to promote mutual learning and exchanges, deepen mutual understanding and friendship, advance our respective modernization drives, and together build a community with a shared future for humanity,” Guo said.

articles.title: Senate probes LPG exports amid domestic supply shortage
articles.summary:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

The Senate has raised concerns over inadequate Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) supply to the domestic market, questioning export figures and arrangements amid efforts to reduce the cost of cooking gas in the country.

The Senate Committee on Gas Resources, chaired by Jarigbe Jarigbe, raised the concerns during an interface with stakeholders in the gas sector at the National Assembly in Abuja.

The meeting examined LPG exports, revenue remittances and the availability of cooking gas for local consumption, with lawmakers seeking explanations for the supply shortfall and its implications for consumers.

Jarigbe said the situation undermined the government’s efforts to ease the burden of rising cooking gas prices on Nigerians, citing Presidential Executive Order 9, signed by President Bola Tinubu on February 13, 2026.

“LPG has to be supplied to the domestic market for the good of the common man as intended with Executive Order 9 issued by President Tinubu to ameliorate the sufferings of the masses on price of gas,” he said.

The senator, however, acknowledged that industry operators had raised concerns about the composition of LPG produced, particularly the ratio of propane to butane, which they said influenced export decisions.

He argued that the composition could be adjusted through blending to make the product more suitable for local consumption.

“And they give an excuse that the ratio of propane to butane is 80-20, and that’s what they export. But it’s a matter of blending, so that it will be the reverse: the quantity of butane will be 80%, while the quantity of propane will be 20% for local consumption in Nigeria,” he said.

Speaking after the meeting, Jarigbe said the committee was determined to establish the reasons for the shortage and pursue measures to increase domestic supply and bring down prices.

“We are already working for Nigerians here, for our people, and that’s why we want to get to the root of it,” he said.

“And we’ll make sure that the price of gas goes down, because when there is adequate supply in response to demand, the price will naturally go down.”

At the hearing, the Nigeria Customs Service presented export figures showing that 190.8 metric tonnes of LPG were exported in 2024, while 32.8 metric tonnes were recorded in 2025, bringing the cumulative volume for the two years to 223.699 metric tonnes.

The representative of the service, Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Tariff and Trade, Caroline Kemen Niagwan, said the agency had no record of LPG exports at Escravos in 2026.

She explained that exports required clearance certificates from the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, as well as declarations by exporters through the Customs automated system.

“For the 2026 export of LPG at Escravos, our system showed no records of export because, for you to make an export, there must be an export clearance certificate sent to us by the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, which we send to the commands, and the exporter must make a declaration on our system, which is automated,” she said.

“When we profiled our system, we didn’t have any exports in the whole of 2026. We only had for 2024 and 2025.”

Niagwan further disclosed that approved LPG export volumes stood at 400 metric tonnes for the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and 386.4 metric tonnes for Chevron.

However, a representative of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Enorense Amadasun, explained that the offshore facility at Escravos was originally designed to accommodate LPG evacuation for export.

He said the facility operates under a joint venture between the Federal Government, represented by NNPCL, and Chevron, with export arrangements already in place.

Amadasun said the commission had engaged the operator to explore opportunities to redirect some of the LPG to the domestic market.

He disclosed that Chevron had, in 2024, issued a public request inviting Nigerian LPG off-takers to discuss arrangements for supplying the local market.

“Having said that, when we got this request, we decided to engage the operator to get more details, and that was when we were made to understand that Chevron had actually put out a public request sometime in 2024, to request for Nigeria LPG off-takers to come for them to discuss the possibility to working with some of them to see how they can work it to change some of this to the domestic market,” he said.

A member of the committee, Aniekan Bassey, said the hearing offered lawmakers an opportunity to examine accountability, regulation and the management of petroleum resources.

In a statement after the meeting, Bassey reaffirmed commitment to legislative interventions that would promote transparency, strengthen institutional accountability and protect Nigeria’s economic interests.

The committee is expected to resume its engagement with stakeholders next Tuesday.

articles.title: Plateau govt condemns deadly attack on Tafi Gani community in Miango District
articles.summary:
From Jude Owuamanam, Jos

The Plateau State Government has strongly condemned the deadly attack on Tafi Gani community in Miango District, Bassa Local Government Area.

In a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Communication, Joyce Lohya Ramnap, the government decried the wanton killing of innocent citizens and the destruction of property, which had left families devastated and the entire community in deep anguish.

The government directed security operatives to take strategic action for the protection of lives and property across the affected area.

The government said that, with the return of relative calm, it would continue to work closely with security agencies, traditional institutions and other relevant stakeholders to strengthen security and pursue lasting peace across the state.

The statement said: “The Government of Plateau State shares in their grief and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and the entire Miango community over this tragic loss.

“While appealing to residents to remain calm, vigilant and law-abiding, the Government is appealing to citizens against reprisals, inflammatory statements and the spread of unverified information capable of escalating tensions. Residents are encouraged to cooperate with security agencies and provide credible information that could assist ongoing investigations and security operations.

“The ‘Time is Now’ Administration under the leadership of His Excellency, Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, Esq., assures the people that it will not relent in its responsibility to safeguard every citizen, irrespective of ethnic, religious or political affiliation.”

US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has undercut US President Donald Trump's assertion earlier this month that he "won't be paying Israel" by the end of this year.

Huckabee, the former governor of Arkansas who is an evangelical pastor and a staunch Zionist - by his own description - said on Tuesday at a conference in Tel Aviv that he's "not certain that there will be a cessation on an abrupt basis by the end of this year". 

That's because Washington currently gives Israel $3.8bn a year, in a 10-year memorandum of understanding that runs from 2019 to 2028.

The package also includes $3.3bn in foreign military financing and $500m in cooperative missile defence programmes.

articles.title: Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports
articles.summary:
Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 21:13

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman expected to travel to the US next month for G-20 in first trip since start of war

This aerial photograph shows a view of the Riyadh skyline on 23 November 2026

Off

Fresh explosions rocked Riyadh on Wednesday as Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, as the kingdom’s deterrence and defensive capabilities continue to be challenged.

The Houthis said that both strikes on the ports “resulted in damage” while the Saudi-led coalition acknowledged that a projectile hit the port of Jazan, resulting in minor damage and no casualties.

The port strikes followed an attack on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery. Argus Media, which covers commodity markets, said the Houthis landed two successful blows on the facility, one at the refinery and one at the export terminal. The Houthis say they bombed Ras Tanura as retaliation for the Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah controlled by the group.

Saudi Arabia is shooting down the majority of Houthi missiles and drones fired at it, Arab and Western officials tell Middle East Eye, but it has failed to protect key assets like energy facilities, financial centres and airports.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has tried to rally the US and regional states to his side. Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey and Syria have all sent or committed to delivering military support to Saudi Arabia, but with the exception of Syria - which has sent drone operators - the assistance is defensive.

The Crown Prince met US Central Command chief admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of forces in the Middle East, last week. MEE first reported the planned meeting, which was the third since fighting with the Houthis resumed in July.

The US, Saudi Arabia's top military supplier, however has not publicly committed additional support to the kingdom, although it has troops and advisers inside the country.

Iran tensions simmer

Semafor reported on Wednesday that Mohammed bin Salman will travel to the US next month for the G-20 summit in Miami. Diplomats have speculated for months whether the de facto leader of Saudi Arabia would leave the kingdom amid Houthi strikes and the chances of a new US-Israeli attack on Iran.

'Turn on the weapons spigot': Saudi Arabia asks partners for gear to deter Houthis

Read More »

Tensions between the US and Iran have been simmering for months, with the two sides exchanging blows in the Strait of Hormuz and at some land targets. The US has conducted strikes on Iran’s mainland while Tehran has responded with attacks on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Iran said on Wednesday that an oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in a "restricted zone" in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.

Brent, the international oil benchmark, was up 2.5 percent on Wednesday, trading at $84 per barrel.

The Trump administration says that it is not interested in resuming the war on Iran for now, and instead wants to use economic means to collapse the government, mainly through a blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran has been hit by debilitating inflation, although regional officials who have traveled to the capital have reported busy restaurants and a sense of calm. Fars said on Wednesday that a substantial shipment of dollar banknotes had entered Iran from a neighbouring country.

Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem on Wednesday demanded the immediate release of five men identified as members of the Lebanese movement and accused of forming an armed cell.

Speaking in a televised address broadcast by Hezbollah's Al-Manar channel, Qassem said the men had "done nothing wrong" and "must be released immediately".

Security forces had detained the five earlier this month in a mountainous area in northern Lebanon, a predominantly Christian region far from Hezbollah's main strongholds.

A judge on Wednesday ordered their continued detention pending investigation, a judicial source told AFP.

"We are being patient in order to preserve civil peace, but patience in the face of injustice has limits," Qassem warned, adding the group would "push back against danger" if necessary.
